title: DR1 asks nothing at all about identifying a commodity that has no identifier type of its own; the frontend asks for free-text identification details and an animal description instead.

finding.frontend: Every commodity gets an identification record. Where the commodity is on none of the four identifier allowlists — of the five commodities the frontend offers, that is Fish — the record falls back to two free-text fields, 'Identification details' (hinted 'Any other way this animal is identified, if it has no passport, tattoo or ear tag') and 'Animal description'. fe-animal-identification-fish is that page: a salmon line headed 'Fish (0301) — Salmo salar', with those two boxes and no others, asking a person to say in prose how one fish out of a consignment is told from the next. The fallback obligations apply by the inverse gate at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:174-198, and the person must still enter one record per animal counted before the task can complete.
finding.prototype: DR1 asks for identification only where the commodity has a typed identifier set. Ornamental fish carries an empty identifier list (app/data/commodities.js:281-284), so it gets no panel, and there is no free-text fallback anywhere in DR1. On a consignment where no commodity has identifiers the page does not exist for that person at all: the identification task row is dropped from the notification overview and a request for the page redirects on to additional details.
finding.difference: Two changes travel together and both are needed for the page to behave as DR1 does. Drop the identificationDetails and description obligations so a commodity with no typed identifier gets no fields, and make the identification page and its hub task row conditional on at least one commodity line having a typed identifier — today the page is always reachable and the unit-record count rule still demands one record per animal. Check what the at-least-one-identifier rule on the unit record means once the fallbacks are gone: a fish line would have no identifier obligation able to satisfy it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a free-text identification or description field rendered on any DR1 identification panel, or a DR1 identification panel rendered for a commodity whose identifier list is empty.
finding.correction: Both halves check out. DR1: fourteen of its twenty-one commodities carry an empty identifier list, ornamental fish among them (app/data/commodities.js:280-290), and nothing in DR1 offers a free-text identifier of any kind. The claim that a direct request for the page redirects on is true and is worth pinning down, because the guard that would obviously do it does not — redirectIfNoAnimalIdentifiers (app/routes.js:1252-1254) returns false and is never called. The redirect is inside the renderer instead: renderAnimalIdentificationDetailsPage returns res.redirect('/additional-animal-details') when hasAnimalIdentifiersRequired is false (app/routes.js:8893-8897), which covers both the GET and every re-render after a post. The dropped task row is at app/routes.js:5777-5781 and the dropped journey step at :1265-1267. Two notes on scope rather than truth. The difference slot opens 'Two changes travel together' and the second of them — making the hub task row conditional — is already its own finding, hub--identification-task-always-shown, which says in as many words that what the page should ask of such a commodity is left to this one. The two overlap and a dependency link is added; whoever schedules them should take the hub row from that finding and the page's fields and redirect from this one. Also, neither named control exists on the captured frontend screen, because the captured line is a cow: the crop will not resolve, and confirming the fallback fields render needs a Fish line. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: the Fish line was driven and shot as fe-animal-identification-fish after this finding was written, and it confirms the frontend slot exactly. Both named controls now resolve on a captured screen — `animalIdentifierIdentificationDetails-0` labelled 'Identification details' with the hint the finding quotes word for word, and `animalIdentifierDescription-0` labelled 'Animal description' — so the crops render and the fallback no longer has to be taken on trust. The page holds no other identifier field, which is the other half of the claim: the inverse gate really does replace the typed set rather than adding to it. Confidence raised from medium to high. What the capture cannot show is DR1's side, and by the nature of the claim it never will — DR1's answer to a commodity with no identifier set is that no panel exists, so there is no DR1 screen to photograph. That half rests on ornamental fish carrying an empty identifier list in app/data/commodities.js and on the redirect inside renderAnimalIdentificationDetailsPage, both re-read in the first pass.

relatedTo.why: that finding owns making the hub task row conditional; this one owns the fields on the page and the redirect when no commodity has identifiers
